text:
alex: Heads up — seeing a big NVMe write IOPS spike in us-west-2 gpu pool starting ~14:18 UTC, several provisioning jobs stuck Pending. Node drains look normal but local disk latencies go through the roof.

mira: Ack, any link to the dashboard or logs?

alex: https://grafana.redwood/infinite/dashboard/321?orgId=1 panel=nvme_iops (shared). quick paste of iostat around the time:
```
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s rrqm/s wrqm/s r_await w_await  aqu-sz  await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         102.5  1854.3   2048  512000    0.00   12.00   0.15   6.02   1.23  6.17   5.40  98.5
```

alex: scrubber (ephemeral-cleaner) started 14:17:34 on ~60% of GPUs and concurrency is at default 8. Correlation looks tight.

devon: That explains the provisioning stalls — kubelet can't write checkpoints fast enough, pods Pending on NodeCondition DiskPressure transiently. Immediate mitigation: reduce scrubber concurrency to 2 and add a rate limit per node.

mira: We saw two instances with "blk_update_request: I/O error" around the same time — possible wear or transient corruption?

toni: If we throttle too much we'll backlog cleanup and risk running out of ephemeral space. Need a balanced approach: prefer prioritizing GPU-serving processes over background scrub.

sam: What about label-based scheduling to avoid running scrub on nodes with active GPU allocations? quick patch: add selector: avoid-label "gpu:active" to cleaner daemonset.

alex: Good call. For immediate action I propose: 1) set cleaner concurrency=2, 2) add rate_limit_mbps=100, 3) add nodeSelectorAvoid for label gpu:active, 4) roll to 10% of nodes as canary.

mira: Post the exact config we would deploy so infra team can apply patch.

alex: posting suggested config snippet:
```
# ephemeral-cleaner config
concurrency = 2
rate_limit_mbps = 100
avoid_node_label = "redwood/gpu-active"
target_labels = ["pool=gpu-us-west-2"]
canary_percent = 10
```

devon: +1. Also add a soft backoff: if nvme.%util > 85% then pause cleaner for 20m. We have a small controller we can add that reads node metrics.

toni: Note on corruption — please collect `/var/log/kern.log` and `dmesg` from hosts that reported I/O errors. If this repeats across many drives we may need to schedule a replacement window.

alex: I pulled dmesg from node gpu-w-022:
```
[14:17:36] nvme nvme0: pci_irq_vector_setup failed -110
[14:17:36] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456
[14:18:01] EXT4-fs error (device nvme0n1): ext4_journal_check_start: Detected aborted journal
```

infra-bot: ALERT: Disk IO anomaly — group=us-west-2-gpu, peak_util=98.5%, affected_nodes=18, incidents_created=0

sam: I'll open a quick runbook entry for the rollback plan and track nodes we patch.

mira: Cost note — if we shift more workloads to S3-backed checkpointing to avoid local writes we'll incur network egress and S3 PUTs. Estimate: ~0.3c per checkpoint * 1000 daily -> ~$3/day but reduces risk. Worth discussing if this becomes a recurring mitigation.

devon: For rollout plan: patch config in staging, deploy to 5 nodes, monitor P50 write latency and NodeCondition counts for 30m, then ramp to 50% if stable. If any node reports blk errors during canary, abort and cordon for diagnostics.

alex: I'll prepare the PR for the cleaner and an ops runbook for canary rollback. tagging @mira for logs collection.

toni: I'll schedule a maintenance window tonight 02:00 UTC to run a bucketed nvme health scan (smartctl + firmware check) for the worst 10 nodes if we keep seeing repeats.

alex: Action items: alex -> PR + canary deploy; devon -> add soft backoff controller; sam -> runbook; mira -> collect logs from 18 nodes; toni -> maintenance scheduling. Re-check in 45m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

mira: Got it. Will start log pulls now.

alex: Thanks all :thumbsup:
